dish: Dry bak chor mee with slow-braised mushroom, pork lard & premium vinegar
n: Seng Kee Mushroom Minced Meat Noodle
address: Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, #01-36, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945
w: A 40-plus-year mushroom minced-meat noodle stall — dry mee pok balanced with a house chilli, deep slow-braised mushroom sauce and crispy pork lard, plus a fish-maw soup its regulars swear by. One of Serangoon Garden Market's most cited names.

dish: Wanton mee with in-house char siew, dumplings & ikan-bilis broth
address: Chomp Chomp Food Centre, #01-12, 20 Kensington Park Road, S557269
w: A humble 50-year wanton mee tucked in a back corner of Chomp Chomp (no relation to the bakery of the same name) — springy noodles, silky-skinned wantons and char siew all made in-house, in a broth with robust ikan-bilis notes.

dish: Charcoal chicken wings & satay, served till 2am
n: Wang Da Shen Chicken Wing & Satay
address: Chomp Chomp Food Centre, 20 Kensington Park Road, S557269
w: One of Chomp Chomp's newer stalls (opened during the pandemic) and the only one that stays open till 2am — charcoal-grilled chicken wings and satay for the deep-supper crowd at Serangoon Gardens.

n: Fa Ji Minced Meat Fishball Noodle
address: Kovan 209 Market & Food Centre, #01-05, 209 Hougang Street 21, S530209
w: The most popular of Kovan 209's three fishball-noodle stalls — springy noodles tossed with handmade fishballs, fishcake and minced pork, a heartland breakfast regular.

dish: Nasi lemak sets, mee rebus, mee siam, lontong & soto
address: Kovan 209 Market & Food Centre, #01-53, 209 Hougang Street 21, S530209
w: Kovan 209's go-to Malay-Muslim stall — nasi lemak sets alongside hawker staples like mee rebus, mee siam, lontong and soto, the halal anchor of the food centre.

dish: Artisanal gelato incl. the putu-mayam 'King Pin' cone
w: The Kovan branch of homegrown gelateria Tom's Palette, opened March 2024 and open till midnight, known for adventurous flavours and a putu-mayam-topped cone nodding to the area's coconut-plantation past. Honest note: after 21 years, both Tom's Palette outlets are set to close in October 2026.

dish: All-day brunch, black-sesame tart & pandan-coconut waffle
w: A Kovan brunch stalwart a short walk from the MRT and one of the few dog-friendly cafes in the area — hearty brunch plates, truffle linguine and desserts like the oozy goma black-sesame tart and Lola's chocolate cake.
A minimalist neighbourhood cafe in Kovan serving a focused menu of Korean-leaning fusion food, bingsu desserts and hand-crafted beverages — a modern counterpoint to the estate's old-school stalls.

dish: Trademarked durian mousse on ice among 50+ Chinese desserts
w: A Serangoon Gardens dessert institution on the second floor of a shophouse — famous for its trademarked durian mousse served on ice with a dollop of durian flesh, one of 50-plus traditional Chinese desserts.

dish: Cantonese-Teochew zi char & dim sum from an ex-Lei Garden chef
address: myVillage @ Serangoon Garden, #02-01, 1 Maju Avenue, S556679
w: A family-style Cantonese-Teochew restaurant at myVillage helmed by ex-Lei Garden head chef Tony Wong (40-plus years, credited as the original creator of mango sago with pomelo) — hearty zi char and a full dim sum spread.

dish: KL-style dry chilli ban mian with hae-bee chilli
w: A KL-style chilli ban mian in an Upper Serangoon Road coffee shop, open into the small hours — al-dente noodles with minced pork, ikan bilis, fried shallots, a runny egg and a fierce dried-shrimp chilli that draws the supper crowd.

dish: Affordable Isaan & Bangkok-street Thai — pandan chicken, pineapple fried rice
w: The pioneer of affordable neighbourhood Thai in Kovan (since 2008), the most popular eatery on Hougang Street 21 — a near-constant queue for pandan chicken, green curry, mango salad and pineapple fried rice at hawker prices.

dish: Curry fish head, otah & home-style zi char
w: A family-run Kovan zi char eatery famed for its fragrant curry fish head, otah and the home-style dishes the family fancies — a low-key neighbourhood favourite off Hougang Street 21.

A Hougang corner-stall congee institution with a perpetual 30-minute queue — thick, hearty bowls of smooth Cantonese-style porridge piled with generous ingredients, warming Hougang residents for decades.

dish: Traditional Teochew cuisine — steamed fish, braised goose & Teochew classics
address: 756 Upper Serangoon Road, #01-15/16 Upper Serangoon Shopping Centre, S534626
w: An authentic family-run Teochew restaurant on Upper Serangoon Road — steamed fish, braised goose and duck, oyster omelette and the mui-and-porridge classics — a fitting anchor for the district's Teochew ('Au Kang') heritage.
